customManagers.description: Pinned CLI/tool versions declared as ARG *_VERSION in the devlaptop and provisioner images, annotated with a `# renovate:` datasource hint on the preceding line.
Kaniko builder image pinned in Helm values and the controller's generated values template.

oauth2-proxy — THE authentication gate for every workspace and the admin console. Pinned tag+digest in both chart templates; the Helm tests assert the same string, so they are listed here too and must bump together or CI fails. See issue #567.

The cosign-signed provisioner image the cluster-privileged provisioning Job runs (#571/#422), pinned tag+digest in the controller chart values. The digest is what the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy enforces, so without tracking it the pin rots as new provisioner images ship each release.

The always-on keeper image (#728), pinned tag+digest as keeper.image in the workspace chart values once the first release publishes it. It holds a token that can scale the workspace, so the pin must follow new signed releases.
The Go version the keeper's CI job tests with, annotated with a `# renovate:` hint — kept in step with the golang builder image in keeper/Dockerfile (grouped below).

packageRules.description: browser-dockerfile/Dockerfile is deprecated and kept for reference only. Its base image is in a private registry Renovate has no credentials for, so looking it up only produced a `No docker auth found` warning on the dependency dashboard every run.
Group the devlaptop + provisioner image CLI/tool bumps into one weekly PR.
Kaniko builder image — pin tag + digest, keep on its own.
oauth2-proxy — the auth boundary. Never batch it with anything else, and label it security so it is reviewed as such, not as routine dependency noise.

Provisioner image — runs under the cluster-privileged provisioner SA and is admission-pinned by digest. Keep it on its own and label security so bumps are reviewed as supply-chain changes, not routine noise.
Keeper image — runs beside every workspace with a token that can stop and start it. On its own and labelled security, like the provisioner.
The keeper's Go toolchain: the golang builder image and the CI go-version move together, so CI tests on the Go that builds the release.
Base OS/node images — pin + track digests together.
Pin and update GitHub Actions by digest, grouped.
SPA/controller dev dependencies are low-risk — batch them.

Expo SDK pins react, react-dom and react-native to exact versions (react-native's renderer is built for one React release). Bumping them alone fails expo-doctor and can crash the app with 'Incompatible React versions', so they move only with an Expo SDK upgrade (`npx expo install --fix`), never as their own PR. See #844.

code-server tags are v-prefixed but CODE_SERVER_VERSION is bare. Every bump must also re-pin the two .deb SHA-256 ARGs or the image build fails its sha256sum -c, so a postUpgradeTask recomputes them from GitHub's release API. The command only runs once the self-hosted run allows it (RENOVATE_ALLOWED_COMMANDS in .github/workflows/renovate.yml; allowedCommands is global-only, so it cannot live here). Until then the PR notes say to run the script by hand.
prBodyNotes: **code-server bump:** the `.deb` SHA-256 pins must move with the version or the image build fails `sha256sum -c`. If this PR did not already update `CODE_SERVER_SHA256_AMD64`/`_ARM64`, run `node scripts/renovate/code-server-sha.mjs` on this branch and push.

packageRules.description: dsh and the npm overrides that patch its pinned dependencies (devlaptop/Dockerfile, #851) move together and need the ACP re-check, so they get their own group and a reminder instead of riding along with the weekly CLI bump.
prBodyNotes: **dsh bump checklist** (see the comment above `ARG DSH_VERSION` in devlaptop/Dockerfile): drop every `DSH_OVERRIDE_*` the new dsh no longer needs, since a stale override silently pins an older version; then repeat the ACP check (`dsh --profile acp` answering `initialize`, opening a session, and resuming one made by the previous version) before merging.

packageRules.description: The dsh overrides only take security fixes within the line dsh was verified against; a major undici/fflate/MCP-client jump needs its own ACP verification, not a routine PR.

The image's Node versions are deliberate: node-dist is the runtime every CLI uses, and node22-dist is the separate Node only dsh runs on. Keep their digests and minor/patch releases current, but a major (e.g. 22 -> 24) is a runtime change that needs its own verification, not a weekly PR.

npm in the image runs on the image's Node (node-dist, Node 20), so its majors move with that runtime: npm 12 needs Node >= 22.22 and would break the build. Minor/patch releases (where npm's own security fixes land) stay tracked.
